title: Vector

evidence.layout: Pointer table at CPU $F400, 50 phrases, each a 4-byte (start, end) record.
evidence.independent_check: The board's own firmware was run and the byte stream it sends the TMS captured and located back in the ROM. It plays 51 streams from 50 distinct addresses spanning $C000-$EE75. Every one of those streams falls inside a phrase this layout converts.
evidence.conversion: 2287 frames converted, all keeping their frame kind when the output was re-parsed with the target tables.
evidence.emulation: The converted devices were loaded into a simulation of the Squawk & Talk board, which booted and issued the same 16 SPEAK EXTERNAL commands as the original set.
evidence.not_verified: No converted ROM from this profile has been played on a real board. Nobody has heard it.
evidence.traced_check: The firmware was driven through every command its MPU can send and played 51 streams from 50 distinct addresses. Each was located back in the ROM and trimmed at its own stop frame, and all 51 fall inside a phrase this layout converts. The addresses are listed so anyone holding these dumps can re-derive them and compare. Compare in device offsets, not CPU addresses: a 2 KB part answers at two.
evidence.not_established_by_the_trace: Every phrase this layout declares was played by the firmware and located in the ROM. No entry rests on the pointer table alone.

notes: This sound ROM set is shared by 4 game revisions: vector, vector4, vectora, vectorb.
The table stores both bounds of every phrase as a 4-byte (start, end) record, not a list of starts.
